articles.title: The Web Can't Afford a JavaScript Runtime Monoculture
articles.summary: Deno's planned end of runtime development narrows the major server-side JavaScript choices to Node.js, Bun, and Cloudflare's workerd. Historical examples from Internet Explorer and the io.js fork show how independent implementations can prevent stagnation and push features into competing runtimes.

articles.title: Measuring Soft Navigation Web Vitals
articles.summary: Sentry's JavaScript SDK v11 measures LCP, CLS, and INP for client-side navigations, exposing slow routes that initial page-load metrics miss. Support currently requires Chromium 151 or later, and the scores should be filtered separately from page loads because their clocks start at different points.

articles.title: Optimizing the sh*t out of TanStack Start
articles.summary: A TanStack Start site improved its mobile Lighthouse score from 73 to 100 and reduced LCP from 5.2 seconds to 1.7 seconds by removing unnecessary JavaScript, images, and font data. More complex changes added maintenance without clearly explaining the final score, making basic asset reductions and regression budgets the more useful starting point.

articles.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default
articles.summary: Benchmarks of large dropdowns and checkbox lists across ten design systems trace slow interactions to repeated layout work, slot handling, and per-checkbox animations. Published Playwright tests enforce timing budgets so shared components can catch performance regressions before they reach every consuming app.

articles.title: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World
articles.summary: Spawn reports shipping 77,000 substantial changes in 30 days with a ten-person team and $3.1 million in token spending, using permanent agents that own parts of the company. Its approach combines direct production feedback, frequent tests, hourly deployments, and fast recovery, with hard-coded gates for irreversible actions. Humans focus on product taste and ambitious changes that agents rarely propose themselves.

articles.title: Radix: 3D Gaussian Splats for the Web (Website)
articles.summary: Radix stores 3D Gaussian splats in typed-array tables on the CPU and GPU and renders them through three.js. Its examples run on WebGPU with a WebGL2 fallback, and the site includes source code, documentation, and ready-to-run scenes.

articles.title: wterm (Website)
articles.summary: wterm renders a terminal into the DOM, providing native text selection, browser find, and screen reader support. It offers React, Vue, and Svelte bindings, pluggable Zig/WASM or Ghostty cores, and WebSocket transport for connecting to a PTY backend.

articles.title: ElementaryUI (Website)
articles.summary: ElementaryUI brings declarative Swift interfaces to the browser through WebAssembly, with SwiftUI-inspired syntax and reactive state. It supports Embedded Swift for small bundles and uses Vite for hot reload during development.

articles.title: Project Speed
articles.summary: Owner rebuilt infrastructure serving more than 10,000 restaurant websites with Astro, selective React, and edge caching. Menu-page p75 LCP fell from 5.4 seconds to 0.7 seconds, while the rollout raised per-restaurant revenue by more than 4%.

articles.title: How fast can you actually patch Ruby?
articles.summary: A comparison of Ruby 4.0.9 availability tracks the gap between a security release and its arrival in installers, container images, CI providers, and hosting platforms. Core-team tools shipped within minutes, while the default Docker image took almost 16 hours and some cloud runtimes took days, showing why teams need to audit the entire update path.

articles.title: Pico CSS Is No Longer Maintained
articles.summary: Pico CSS has been archived, with version 2.1.1 designated as the final release. Existing npm packages, the CDN, and documentation remain available, while the MIT license allows community forks under different names.

articles.title: Node.js 26 LTS Is Generally Available on Vercel
articles.summary: Node.js 26 is now Vercel's default for new projects, and existing projects whose engines.node range permits it upgrade on their next deployment.

articles.title: A Better Way to Handle Select Behaviour
articles.summary: The customizable native select introduces a shared interaction model through appearance: base-select, reducing the need to reproduce conflicting Mac and Windows conventions.

articles.title: Thank you, but I prefer it my way
articles.summary: LLMs make rewriting libraries easier than collaborating on them, raising the risk of fragmented projects, and weakening the incentives to contribute improvements upstream.

articles.title: If IPv4 Were Land (Website)
articles.summary: An interactive cartogram resizes countries by their share of locatable IPv4 addresses, using October 2026 geolocation data.
